subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode repair lands, should OpenClaw accept `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, the transitive `node-pty` install script, and the SDK's argv-carried base64 config transport for this first-party external sandbox plugin?
rationale: This choice authorizes a native dependency graph and sandbox-policy transport boundary; CI and ClawSweeper can detect and repair code issues but cannot approve that security/supply-chain boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Approve final dependency boundary
options.body: After the full-mode guard is fixed, a secops/admin owner approves the exact head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport as acceptable for this prerelease plugin.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Do not merge until the MXC SDK provides a non-argv config transport or maintainers collect stronger boundary evidence.

options.title: Keep MXC outside first-party distribution
options.body: Decline the first-party plugin path and let MXC continue as a contributor-owned external package if the native dependency boundary is not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Approve final dependency boundary
recommendation.body: After the full-mode guard is fixed, a secops/admin owner approves the exact head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport as acceptable for this prerelease plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS names this team for dependency guard, lockfile, shrinkwrap, and sandbox/security-sensitive surfaces touched by this PR.
